content.summary_of_the_paper: The method presents a deterministic type of auto-encoder model, where instead of computing posterior expectations by drawing reparameterized samples, they use sigma points from the unscented transform.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
To my mind, this formulation is not solid: when you are dealing with latent variables, for which a posterior must be learned, you need to optimize an ELBO. ELBO means posterior expectations; posterior expectations means sampling, that is a form of stochasticity taken into consideration (unless an analytical expression is available). The "samples" from the unscented transform kill this notion of stochasticity.

Therefore, the method should be put on a different basis from the theoretical point of view.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: While the objective function is clear, the method has serious conceptual flaws, as I explain above. The idea of using the unscented transform could have been useful under a different viewing angle of autoencoders. The experiments are reproducible to some extent.

display_title: Deterministic autoencoders in the context of the ELBO

content.title: Deterministic autoencoders in the context of the ELBO
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for their comments and appreciate that they recognized the novelty of the presented approach. Also, we welcome the challenging of the theoretical foundations of our paper. 

We are aware that the original ELBO formulation involves computation of an expectation (an integral) w.r.t. the posterior distribution. The standard VAE solves the intractable integral using Monte Carlo sampling with one random sample in practice. In contrast, the [Regularized Autoencoder (RAE)](https://openreview.net/forum?id=S1g7tpEYDS), published at ICLR 2020, is still motivated from the standard ELBO but with an additional assumption of a constant variance posterior and a constraint in the decoder outputs between any two draws from the posterior ([Appendix B in the RAE paper](https://openreview.net/attachment?id=S1g7tpEYDS&name=original_pdf#page=12)). The constant variance assumption allows to drop the entropy term of the KL divergence ($\mathcal{L}_\text{KL} = \mathcal{L}_\text{CE} - \mathcal{L}_\text{E}$) in the standard ELBO formulation. Thus, one obtains an autoencoder that requires no sampling or stochasticity in training while still achieving competitive results on image modeling tasks.  

The Unscented Autoencoder (UAE) model is in the same class of deterministic autoencoders as the RAE. The key difference in our derivation from the ELBO (Section 5.2 and Appendix C in our paper) is that we incorporate no constant-variance restrictions on the posterior and are able to model uncertainty in the latent space. In other words, we derive a more general deterministic autoencoder that is also motivated by the ELBO. Furthermore, we incorporate sampling of the posterior but in a different way to the reparameterization trick. We generate a biased, deterministically-selected subset of samples from the posterior. In this way, we replace the high-variance unbiased sampling with low-variance biased sampling, which has been shown to work well in the Unscented Kalman Filter context. We will improve our presentation of this concept in Section 4.2 "Unscented Transform in the VAE". 

Once again, we thank the reviewer for their criticism that improves the quality of our paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose modifications to the standard VAE architecture for image generation with the aim of improving Frechet Inception distance of generated images. This work builds upon  [Ghosh et.al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.12436.pdf) who first proposed a deterministc re-interpretation of training VAEs. This paper takes a similar problem, reinterpreting VAE traiing, and proposes multiple alternative tricks to train VAEs. The empirical evaluation also follows [Ghosh et.al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.12436.pdf) and shows improved FID scores.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strengths
- writing is clear
- ablation studies look positive

# Weaknesses
It seems this paper builds upon [Ghosh et.al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.12436.pdf), yet somewhat

### Why use gradient regularization and unscentedness?
Ghosh et.al. explicitly tried to remove stochasticity and replaced it with analytic regularization about the posterior mean, this paper uses stochastic estimation and applies regularization about randomly chosen sigma point (i.e. not the posterior mean). Is this not redundant or regularising the wrong part of the latent space?

### Theoretical Motivation for Unscentedness
The reparameterization trick samples $\epsilon \sim N(0, 1)$ and $z = \mu + L\epsilon$ where $LL^T = \Sigma$. The proposed method restricts the generated sample $z$ to opposing pairs of points on a $\Sigma$ scaled ellipsoid around $\mu$. This is almost mathematically equivalent to the reparameterization trick with restricting $\epsilon$ to be a one-hot vector scaled by $\sqrt n$ with a random sign (like just eigen axis aligned points with constant [Mahalanoubis distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahalanobis_distance)), the proposed reduction in variance does not come from a better estimator or the use of sigma points, it may be interpreted as the reparameterization trick with a handicapped noise generation, it feels rather artificial and a not a real advantage. (The authors do somewhat acknowledge this when discussing "holes" and the interpolation experiment.) Unscented Kalman filter passes multiple points through a funciton and computes the mean and variance of the outputs, this aspect is not used in this work.

### Comparison with Similar Works in Approximate Inference
There has been a lot of work on tweaking the ELBO training objective of a VAE to reduce variance,
- [Importance Weighted AutoEncoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.00519)
- [Debiasing Evidence Approximations: On Importance-weighted Autoencoders and Jackknife Variational Inference](https://openreview.net/forum?id=HyZoi-WRb)
- [Doubly Reparameterized Gradient Estimators
for latent variable models](http://approximateinference.org/2018/schedule/Tucker2018.pdf)

If the author claim to reduce variance by using an off-the-shelf statistical trick, then much of the above literature contains many existing off the shelf statistical tricks for the same purpose yet are not considered.

### Comparison with Similar works in GANs
[Ghosh et.al. 2020](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.12436.pdf) did not provide comparisons with GANs or more advanced VAEs, hence I acknowledge that it may be unfair to ask for more extensive comparisons in this follow up work. However, comparisons with such methods *would* make this paper a lot stronger, if the goal is to make an image generator and abandon any Bayesian-ness (following Ghosh et.al. did), why not compare to other Bayesian-less generators? At present, I feel proposing a method in between VAEs and GANs and avoiding benchmarks with advanced methods from either field weakens the paper, especially since the methodological contribution seems rather incremental.

### Some Results Appear Inconsistent with Prior Work
Maybe I misunderstood, but RAE-SN CelebA results in Ghosh et.al. 2020 have lower FID scores than the result reported here, the REA-GP and RAE-L2 do not seem to match, variability in reproducing results is to be expected, is it possible to include RAE-SN and compute error bars? Otherwise, these results are less convincing. The cifar10 FID scores are completely different to Ghosh et.al. 2020?

## Minor Comments
- replacing the prior KL with the Wasserstein metric violates the information theoretic interpretation of the ELBO and KL divergence, (I believe zero variance equating to infinite KL is a feature, not a bug in this perspective) it would be nice should be more acknowledged.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
### Clarity
- I felt the paper was clear. Although, it seems to heavily rely upon the reader being very familiar with Ghosh et.al. 2020 (e.g. ex post sampling)


### Novelty
- the four claims of novelty: I am not convinced by the value of unscenteness, full covariance is arguably incremental, Wasserstein posterior regularization seems very beneficial in practice, and decoder regularisation is adopted from Ghosh et.al. 2020. I think it is hard to justify acceptance.

### Reproducibility
- the method describes all the mathematical
content.summary_of_the_review:
- well written
- the novelty of the contributions may be incremental: I do not feel unscentedness is well justified.
- numerical results are not entirely consistent with past work
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.title: Response to "Weaknesses" part
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for their structured and insightful comments, especially w.r.t. placing our work in the wider context of the state of the art. We think that emphasizing the novelty of our work is crucial considering the high research activity surrounding VAEs, GANs and diffusion models. In our replies below, we respond to all the points except _Theoretical Motivation for Unscentedness_; we plan to address this at a later point. 

_Why use gradient regularization and unscentedness?_
- The motivation behind regularizing the decoder around the sigma points is removing holes in the latent space. We have observed that for all UT model variants the decoder gradient penalty (GP) boosts the performance. To gain more insights, we have performed additional experiments (so far with CIFAR10) with VAE-GP and VAE*-GP, which we will add into the next version of the paper. Since both models perform random sampling, the argument of regularizing the "wrong part of the latent space" could apply to them as well. We have observed that for the VAE, the GP addition makes a negligible difference, while for the VAE*, it provides a ~7% boost. We will extend the ablation study with these additional experiments. 

_Comparison with Similar Works in Approximate Inference_
- We thank the reviewer for pointing out additional works tackling variance reduction; we will extend our Related Work section with these works. The IWAE is known to have the problem of a diminishing gradient signal with multiple samples, despite the reduced variance brought on by the multiple samples in the first place. Compared to the IWAE, we take a single sample. The two additional works use IWAE as a foundation and mainly directly address its issues. The Jackknife Variational Inference reduces the bias of the estimator while potentially increasing the variance compared to the vanilla IWAE and the standard ELBO estimator. The concrete difference of our approach is that we use an explicitly biased procedure that reduces the gradient variance. The bias of the method pertains to the estimate of the reconstruction error given the posterior distribution represented by the sigma points (in the regular VAE, this estimate is not biased). Regarding the Doubly-Reparameterized-Gradient-Estimator, we were not aware of it; we thank the reviewer for pointing it out. We think that the same procedure could be applied to the discrete distribution of sigma points to further reduce the variance (with a limit in the number of sigma points). However, the focus of our work was not applying variance reduction techniques in general – we regard it as a side-effect of the model. We aimed to offer a new, sigma-point-based reparameterization that improves the reconstruction quality in the context of the overall model with the proposed loss function components. Furthermore, our aim was to fill a research gap towards deterministic non-variational autoencoders.

_Comparison with Similar works in GANs_
- We agree that a comparison with more advanced models would be beneficial to place the performance of our model in a wider context. Currently, we are implementing the VQ-VAE model and aim to extend the paper with this additional baseline. However, we consider a comparison with vanilla GANs orthogonal to the method since GANs do not have a latent space and are trained adversarially. In principle, we could apply adversarial losses to our method as well (and any other VAE) but we decided to limit ourselves to the space of autoencoders. We consider our model to be in between the VAE and RAE, not in between VAEs and vanilla GANs in general. 

_Some Results Appear Inconsistent with Prior Work_
- In Table 1 of Ghosh et al, the RAE-SN achieves the best result among the RAE models in 6/12 cases, RAE-L2 in 6/12 cases as well, and RAE-GP in 0/12 cases. In the meantime, we have implemented RAE-SN as well, however, the preliminary results show that it performs similarly to RAE-L2 and RAE-GP.  
- Regarding the CIFAR10 scores, we have realized that one of the reasons behind the discrepancy was a very aggressive perturbation that we applied in dataset preprocessing (size-4 padding + random 32x32 crop + random horizontal flip), as opposed to Ghosh et al. With less perturbation, the preliminary results show a 40% improvement consistently across all CIFAR10 scores and bring our results closer to the ones reported in Ghosh et al. Furthermore, there are additional implementation differences in terms of pytorch/tensorflow implementation, which we discuss in Appendix A. Finally, to aid reproducibility, we will add the source code of the models as supplementary material of the paper, as well as making a public repository later.

content.title: Response to "Minor Comments" part
content.comment:
_Replacing the prior KL with the Wasserstein metric violates the information theoretic interpretation of the ELBO and KL divergence, (I believe zero variance equating to infinite KL is a feature, not a bug in this perspective) it would be nice should be more acknowledged._
- We agree with the reviewer's observation and are fully aware of it. With the Wasserstein metric, the resulting loss function is not an ELBO anymore. However, in all our practical experiments, we found that the encoder should be allowed to model peaked distributions (in order to produce sharper images for example) without a high loss that exceeds the reconstruction error. This is allowed by the Wasserstein metric and not by the KL divergence.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors present a new objective to train variational autoencoders by employing the unscented transform to simulate draws from the variational posterior (in lieu of conventionally sampling from a standard normal and reparameterization thereof).
Using the unscented transform the authors argue to achieve a lower-variance estimator of the gradient of the objective which helps training VAEs in particular in high dimensions and by that enables better performance of a VAE wrt generating new data or reconstruction of data.
In addition the method makes several other modifications to the original VAE objective to yield improved performance. The paper elegantly incorporates ideas of previous work on deterministic autoencoders and extends these to fit in their framework.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The papers demonstrates competitive results in terms of reconstruction and generation of data in auto-encoder setting. The benchmarks and ablation studies are convincing. The motivation to construct lower-variance gradient estimators is reasonable.

The paper does in my opinion have no major weaknesses that need to be addressed. There are however some minor comments:
- Since the paper closely follows Ghosh et al. (2019) the authors could have also included the experiments on modelling structured inputs and not only on imaging experiments (this is not a requirement by the reviewer though, but rather a desideratum).
- The authors claim that their estimator is biased. It is not clear to the reviewer why this should necessarily be the case. Is it only because it the sigma-point samples are correlated? The authors could elaborate on this by deriving the estimator's expectation in the appendix.
- Unless it was missed by the reviewer, the means and covariances of the "f-transformed" distributions are never computed. The UT is merely used to define statistics of the posterior. Is this the case? If so, the Eqn 6 seems unnecessary.
- The authors at several points speak of "deterministic sampling". Is choosing a sigma point not effectively also a reparameterization from a discrete uniform RV $i$ to the sigma point $\chi_i$ ?
- The authors limit themselves to benchmark against VAEs/RAEs exclusively, despite several others works on VAEs in the recent past.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is clear, easily understandable and generally well written.  However, in my opinion the paper offers only little novelty (as far as I can tell using the UT to sample from the variational posterior and using the Wasserstein-distance in lieu of the KL-divergence). 

The authors mention that code is only accessible on request. I believe they should open-source it upon acceptance of the paper. The authors stated they were not fully able to reproduce the results of Ghosh et al. (2019): for better reproducibility of their own method 
they consequently should publish the code.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors propose a new objective to train VAEs. The paper makes use of an unscented transform to provide more informative and lower-variance posterior representations and suggests several modifications to the original VAE objective for generative modelling. By that they achieve competitive performance in data generation and reconstruction. In my opinion the overall paper is a good contribution to the community with several convincing experiments and ablation studies albeit with only limited novelty.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a deterministic auto-encoder using the unscented transform (UT). The UT uses a deterministic set of $n$ (sigma) points to estimate the moments of a non-linear transformation of a known random variable.  The authors integrate the UT i the loss function of a deterministic auto-encoder, leading to specifc regularization of the ELBO. Authors also propose a small modification of the loss, substituting KL terms with Wasserstein disstances. Overall the experiments performed show improved performance of the method against alternative formulation, as well as ablation studies (in the Appendix) regarding the different parts of the model.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength:
* Another example of a Deterministic AE  reaching SOTA
* The UT can be used to account for rich(er) covariance structures (compared to the isotropic/diagonals in RAE/VAE)
* Thorough ablation studies (Wasserstein metric, unscented transform sampling, full covariance matrix in the posterior, and the decoder regularization)

## Weakness:
* The method proposed in this work has a lot “moving parts”. Also, there is no clear intuition on 'why' these incremental tweeks should work well together.  
* No clear empirical or theoretical recommendation about how to choose the number of sigma points.
* While the ablation studies are great, authors compare their method against others only on a few datasets (compared, .e.g., to the RAE paper). 


## Additional comments
* What is the impact of the number of sigma points on the performance of the model? In appendix D, Table 4 the results are non-trivial, for example, increasing the number of sigma points leads to an increase and decrease in the loss in some cases.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is well written and clearly motivated. Nonetheless, more of the experiments could be in the main paper.

Quality: The paper is technically sound. Limited experimental campaign compared to prior art (number of datasets), but good  ablation studies.

Novelty: The proposal (UT + deterministic/variational AEs) is novel.

Reproducibility: No code in the supplementary material is available.
content.summary_of_the_review: I like that fact the unscented autoencoders are simple models, yet acheive good performance. While the method here is a mixed-bag of many components (without a clear reason to work well together), there are good ablation studies showing each component leads to some improvement.  That being said, I am leaning towards acceptance.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.

content.title: Withdrawal decision
content.comment:
We thank the reviewers for their comments, suggestions, and criticisms of the paper, especially w.r.t: 
- Recognizing the novelty of the work in regard to the Unscented Transform (UT) and the Wasserstein metric components, as well as their clear presentation, 
- The potential usage of the entire Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)-like procedure within the model compared to using only the input-level UT in its current state, 
- The usage of the per-posterior Wasserstein metric in place of the KL divergence, as a very simple and beneficial practical contribution to the field, 
- The suggestions to extend the evaluation with more advanced baselines and non-image datasets 

We have already started with the suggested improvements and have positive results. However, even though we think that the paper in its current state would be valuable to the community, we decided to withdraw it in order to have more time to address all the concerns. This would not have been possible within the rebuttal period. Therefore, we plan to submit a revised version of the paper at another venue in the near future. In light of the withdrawal, we decided not to reply to the remaining individual reviews. Once again, we thank the reviewers for their valuable feedback that contributes to improving our paper.
